## Route 2b: λ=0, start A, two dielectric branches

**smaller-dV:** limit_reached at 53 iterations, training cost 36.7833961664, common-149 cost 23.0753630456. **larger-dV:** Fit running; no returned result.

## Joint recalibration amendment 2: precursor stops at five bounds

The new [amendment-2 calculation](results/joint-recalibration-170/amendment-2/route1/precursor/README.md), performed on merged Engine `84ca269d`, has **no selected joint precursor**. Start A reaches 40 iterations without convergence; both segment diameters reach 5.8 Å, both Born diameters 1 Å, and R5's unshifted $a_k$ 2400 K, all bounds. No Route 1 B or 3b fit runs after this required stop. Route 2 remains subject to its separately reported native-time/non-convergence stop. All 203 quantities are available at both starts and in the native A vector, with zero failed trials. This is an incomplete calibration attempt with retained diagnostics, not parameter adoption or an EOS impossibility result.

The four [unchanged-record replays](results/joint-recalibration-170/amendment-2/qualification-84ca269d/README.md) pass both $10^{-8}$ limits: maximum relative cost difference $8.42\times10^{-13}$ and weighted-row difference $3.68\times10^{-10}$. One fresh Python 3.13.14 environment pins wheel SHA-256 `98a140a00796782b536c892695b3546547ab5986a4905ae723190aceee38d83a`, NumPy 2.5.4 and SciPy 1.18.1. This is numerical verification of unchanged records.

The [shared inputs](results/joint-recalibration-170/amendment-2/shared/README.md) apply 27.14274817 wt% CO₂-free MEA to Jakobsen 011 and 022, loadings 0.29/0.59, and zero bicarbonate–water interaction. At each state the inorganic numerator is bicarbonate plus carbonate; the denominator is MEA plus MEAH⁺ plus carbamate. Observed pooled ratios are 0.007279344859 and 0.141342756184. Eighteen unchanged Böttinger/Matin quantities and six Jakobsen ratios supply 24 standardized differences. The 16 overlaps with the older 195-target precursor retain this difference definition exactly once, yielding 203 residuals and 115 remaining logarithmic species quantities. Source-mass/seed conservation and the retained D₂O/dioxane approximations are explicit in the frozen requests and checks; historical wrong-feed results below remain history.

The [shared Schreckenberg reduction](results/joint-recalibration-170/amendment-2/stage5-smaller-dV/README.md) passes on all 14 unloaded Agieienko–Buchner compositions at 298.15 K/101325 Pa. The smaller-$d_V$ pair is **0.246454031209 L/mol, 2436.442300727 K**; the larger pair is **0.730988823808 L/mol, 1019.078611017 K**. Rank is 2, condition 6.17608348 and discriminant 3.22393997846. Both native curves reproduce the reduction within $2.85\times10^{-14}$ absolute. Permittivity RMSE is 0.30616047. Both exact full records, scale-based sensitivity and coherent ±1% perturbations are retained. This is dielectric calibration and numerical verification, conditional on fixed water/EOS and the declared neutral-unloaded approximation. The larger pair remains for later work; neither branch is adopted.

Precursor A cost decreases **62.94479652 → 0.5871029140**; B's unfit starting cost is **18.3038169348**. The weighted coordinate-scaled Jacobian has full rank **10/10**, free rank **5/5**, and condition **1078.5353 full / 42.5287 free**. Full/free spectra, native gradients and unavailable covariance are retained. R5 changes **−277.91 K** from source, beyond the declared 80 K reporting magnitude; CO₂ dispersion remains fixed at 169.21 K. Returned CO₂–water $k_p=-0.0481735994649$, $b=-40.4043211794$ K; mutual ion interaction is −0.802917025988. MEAH⁺/carbamate dispersions are 422.7856934/359.5316977 K. The optional same-matrix R5 projection onto all seven ion columns has cosine **0.9996859613** (1.435954°), showing strong local overlap under this objective while full numerical rank remains ten.

### Bounded diagnosis after the precursor stop

The parent-authorized [two-point diagnosis](results/joint-recalibration-170/amendment-2/route1/precursor/diagnosis/README.md) leaves Route 1 stopped. It adds an exact start Jacobian and uses the retained iteration-40 matrix; all 203 start predictions agree exactly and weighted residuals agree within $1.53\times10^{-16}$. This is conditional assessment and numerical verification of an incomplete calibration. No new fit, B start, 3b or bound change runs.

The additive cost by family (25 reacting pressures / 115 unshared species / 39 Kiepe / 24 stage-4 differences) is **0.10330737 / 0.02960787 / 0.00067902 / 62.81120227** at A and **0.06447827 / 0.03486145 / 0.00122766 / 0.48653552** at iteration 40. The diagnostic original 131-species log score is 0.03034724 → 0.03188384; it is not added because its 16 overlapping targets already belong to the stage-4 difference family. The ten largest targets/states and signed contributions of every target to the five bound-coordinate gradients are retained in the diagnosis.

The full weighted, coordinate-scaled condition is **12290.8524 → 1078.5353**, rank ten at both points. All ten columns start free; the five final free columns have condition 42.5287. R5's projection onto seven ion columns has cosine **0.999846708 → 0.999685961** (angles 1.00324° → 1.43595°). This is strong local overlap under the declared weights, without loss of full numerical rank or proof of feasible compensation at the bounds. At iteration 40, MEAH⁺ segment and Born gradients favor movement inward; carbamate segment/Born and R5 favor outward movement. The bound directions therefore have competing local incentives.

Jakobsen 011/022 inorganic-pool standardized residuals are **+48.8892/+13.1110 → +0.9837/+0.3963**; Matin 009/019/016 are **+6.3315/+11.4830/+9.7684 → −1.6192/−0.1907/−1.6941**. The historical stopped ions-first pool residuals are +0.3721/+4.9554 and −1.7390/−1.1321/−3.3588. Historical Jakobsen 022 used the wrong feed; these are conditional discrepancies at different vectors and are not evidence that pooling alone caused an improvement. The report retains predicted values, scales and common-weight comparisons.

Projected gradient is **$6.93615723\times10^{-4}$** against $10^{-8}$, including the feasible inward MEAH⁺ segment direction. The last cost decrease is **$2.95256563\times10^{-6}$**, from 0.587105866588 to 0.587102914023: **cost was still falling**. No complete precursor is selected. **Shared step 2, stage 5 smaller-$d_V$, completed**; its full record remains [parameters.json](results/joint-recalibration-170/amendment-2/stage5-smaller-dV/parameters.json).

The diagnosis charges **47.785628000 CPU-s / 47.792345550 active wall-s**, within 60/60, including the conservatively charged first capture error and short reporting/check commands. The parent keeps Route 1 stopped for its design decision with the owner.

## Historical joint recalibration: initial ion calibration stopped at four bounds

The historical campaign below is superseded for further calibration by [#170 amendment 2](https://github.com/tannerpolley/Amine-Thermodynamics/issues/170#issuecomment-6204801680) on 15 October 2026. The new-wheel qualification and amended calculation are reported above; these earlier statements describe the historical sequence. Neither the superseded 160 K stage-3 vector nor the iteration-40 ion vector is a permitted start or calibration input. Earlier next-step and pending-decision statements below describe the historical calculation; reuse is limited to the inputs and checks explicitly retained by amendment 2.

The historical ions-first amendment fixed CO₂ dispersion at 169.21 K, reset bicarbonate–water interaction from +0.5 to zero, and estimated seven ion quantities on source R2/R5 chemistry and the stage-2 neutral binaries. Engine `cf26a17b` passed all four unchanged-record requalifications at the declared $10^{-8}$ limits. The five unloaded 30 wt% density predictions change by at most $1.37\times10^{-12}$ kg/m³ after the bicarbonate correction; all five numerical closure checks pass.

These historical 26-target calculations used an incorrect CO₂-free MEA mass fraction of 0.11583721405835971 (11.58372141 wt%) for Jakobsen state 022. The subsequent [carbonate diagnosis](results/joint-recalibration-170/stage4/initial-source-chemistry/diagnosis-carbonate/README.md) traced both 011 and 022 to the nominal 30 wt% batch; under the retained D₂O-as-water and omitted-dioxane assumptions, both require 0.2714274817259226 (27.14274817 wt%). The fit and sensitivity numbers below describe the executed wrong-feed declaration. They do not qualify amendment 2's corrected-feed, 24-target pooled declaration.

Both initial ion starts return all nine admitted states and 26 targets. The first A fit uses its 40 iterations without native convergence. Cost falls from **59.17684172 to 1.36097504**, but carbamate segment diameter reaches **2 Å**, carbamate dispersion/k **50 K**, and both Born diameters **1 Å**, all lower bounds. Its other returned values are MEAH⁺ segment diameter 4.49330937 Å, MEAH⁺ dispersion/k 489.25373230 K, and mutual interaction −0.76308270. The mutual change exceeds the 0.03 reporting scale. Full/free ranks are **7/7 and 3/3**, with condition numbers **16199.96 and 147.29**. Native covariance is unavailable for this unconverged, bound-active vector.

| Family | A start mean absolute relative error, % | A unconverged native vector, % |
|---|---:|---:|
| 18 mole-fraction targets | 63.006749 | 16.799706 |
| 8 Jakobsen species/total-amine ratios | 326.773624 | 21.288693 |

These are calibration errors under fixed inputs and declared engineering scales, not physical parameter uncertainty. All 26 native predictions are available, with no failed trials. Endpoint closure, replay and centered derivative checks have not run. The initial application run also encountered a serialization defect: seven tied coordinates return eleven physical parameter-target values. The corrected reader now consumes all eleven, checked on exact native charts at A and iteration 40. No subsequent fit ran; the retained vector is for diagnosis only.

**No I₀ is selected. S₁, I₁, S₂ and the movement test are unrun under the explicit stop rule.** R5 remains at source 2677.91 K, and CO₂–water interaction/slope remain at their stage-2 values. No further start fit, bound change or later stage was launched. The [stage-4 report](results/joint-recalibration-170/stage4/initial-source-chemistry/README.md) retains starts, source declarations, raw fit, error tables, singular spectra, bounds and timings; [wheel requalification](results/joint-recalibration-170/stage4/qualification-cf26a17b/README.md) retains the unchanged comparisons. Its Kiepe isotherm/root tables describe that unchanged-record requalification, not a new stage-3 endpoint.

A parent-authorized [bounded diagnosis](results/joint-recalibration-170/stage4/initial-source-chemistry/diagnosis-chemistry/README.md) evaluates exact ion-plus-chemistry Jacobians without a fit. The two Jakobsen carbonate-ratio targets supply 47.36794 of A’s initial 59.17684 cost; their iteration-40 cost is 0.00192. The remaining error is mainly bicarbonate/pool and protonated-MEA targets. The R5 reference-level sensitivity overlaps strongly with the four bound-active ion columns:

Both nine-column matrices have rank 9 at the declared cutoff. The local R5 cost gradient is positive at both points, so decreasing its fixed source reference level lowers this ion objective to first order. The R2 pivot-preserving enthalpy column is much weaker on these 20/40 °C rows; it does not test the R2 reference level. The zero reactive interactions were not varied. This supports local reaction-reference/activity-coefficient confounding without selecting a unique cause of the four bounds. Cost still falls in the last step, and projected gradient is $1.0774\times10^{-5}$ against $10^{-8}$. Intermediate active-bound membership is unavailable in the retained scalar history.

At the end of the chemistry diagnosis, before the subsequent carbonate diagnosis, cumulative program charges recorded on 15 October 2026, including the authorized diagnosis, are **1289.168845 CPU-s / at least 441.633360 active wall-s**, leaving at that point at most **142710.831155 CPU-s / 21158.366640 wall-s**. # Current working record {#working-record}

**The current record is the investigator-adopted heat-augmented SSM+DS F1 start A, for 30 wt% MEA on a CO₂-free basis at 40–80 °C.** The [#170 owner decision](https://github.com/tannerpolley/Amine-Thermodynamics/issues/170#issuecomment-6071318908) adds eight Vinjarapu integral heats to each F1–F6 fit; the [#147 design amendment](https://github.com/tannerpolley/Amine-Thermodynamics/issues/147#issuecomment-6070624850) fixes the same five interaction coordinates and inherited calibrated chemistry. Water, ion sizes and the density-only empirical volume translation remain fixed.

Pressure calibration covers 40/60 °C, species calibration covers 20–60 °C, and heat calibration uses 40 °C. Evidence is **calibration for the fitted data; prediction for Arcis, 80–120 °C and concentration transfer; no physical validation**. The high-temperature data have historical access and selection ancestry; they are not untouched tests. Concentration transfer and absorber/stripper use are not qualified. **The investigator promoted this record for manuscript writing on 2026-10-08.**

<!-- RESULTS:working-record:BEGIN -->

The current [fit-comparison rows](results/heat-final-170/fit-comparison.csv) give a 149-target objective cost of **32.056684**: 47 pressures, 94 species targets and 8 integral heats. The matched pressure/species subtotal is **30.330866**, against **30.089761** without heat. Fitted pressure AARD is **13.814751%** and species AARD is **7.891434%**. AARD is the average absolute relative deviation; the declared residual scales and conditional errors do not constitute measured uncertainty for all targets.

The displayed layouts therefore give $B$ in K for R1–R4 and $A$ in K for R5; $D$ for R1–R3 and $C$ for R5 are in K⁻¹. Other coefficients are dimensionless. R2/R5 are inherited calibrated chemistry, held fixed in the five-coordinate fit; they are not new source measurements.

Vinjarapu uses eight fitted points at 313.15 K and 1.734 MPa, from zero carbon; Arcis uses 14 predicted points at 322.5 K, separated by pressure. Negative heat denotes exothermic absorption. **A single linear-in-$1/T$ interaction slope cannot satisfy both the 40 °C heats and the 100–120 °C pressures in this retained comparison.** Heat fitting improves calorimetry while the high-temperature pressure deviations increase in both cohorts. This conclusion applies to the fixed chemistry, five fitted coordinates, residual scales and retained observations; it does not establish a general impossibility for another model. The working 40–80 °C interval is not qualification of high-temperature extrapolation or concentration transfer.

# Density and heat capacity

## Density

The adopted record retains a density-only translation, $\rho_{\mathrm{corr}}=M_{\mathrm{mix}}/[v_{\mathrm{EOS}}+10^{-6}c(x_{\mathrm{MEAH^+}}+x_{\mathrm{MEACOO^-}})]$, with $c=39.5142952780$ cm³/mol, calibrated on four Amundsen (2009) Table 3 states. It is not applied to chemical potentials, enthalpy or heat capacity and is not applied automatically by Engine. [corrected-densities.csv](results/heat-final-170/corrected-densities.csv) evaluates the current record at all retained Amundsen loaded-solution states, at an assumed 0.100 MPa, on a CO₂-free basis. Errors are absolute relative deviations from the observed density.

<!-- RESULTS:density:BEGIN -->

| States | n | MEA (wt%) | T (K) | Loading (mol/mol MEA) | Without translation, mean / max (%) | With translation, mean / max (%) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Translation calibration | 4 | 30 | 323.15–343.15 | 0.3–0.4 | 15.23 / 17.57 | 0.19 / 0.25 |
| Other retained states | 64 | 20–40 | 298.15–353.15 | 0.1–0.5 | 11.63 / 32.44 | 0.28 / 0.70 |

<!-- RESULTS:density:END -->

Without the translation the physical model overpredicts density at every retained state, by far more than the translated error, so the translation, not the equation of state, carries the reported densities. The first row is the translation's calibration. The other states entered neither the translation nor the record's parameter fits, so they test the translation outside its calibration. [#183](https://github.com/tannerpolley/Amine-Thermodynamics/issues/183) replaces the translation with density rows in the physical fit. The source locator (Amundsen 2009, Tables 2–4) is stored per row in the CSV. Source pressure is unreported; 0.100 MPa is the modeling assumption. The source's ±0.002 g/cm³ uncertainty for loaded solutions excludes the highest temperatures and loadings and leaves its exact per-row boundary unresolved (pp. 3099–3100).

## Heat capacity

Current equilibrium solution Cp spot checks are retained in [heat-capacity-comparison.csv](results/heat-final-170/heat-capacity-comparison.csv), using the heat F1 rows only. The Hilliard (2008) Appendix G.2 observations use 7 mol MEA/kg water; the model uses 30 wt% MEA on a CO₂-free basis, assumes 101325 Pa and represents nominal unloaded MEA by loading $10^{-5}$.

<!-- RESULTS:heat-capacity:BEGIN -->

| Temperature (K) | Nominal loading (mol/mol MEA) | Cp (kJ/(kg·K)) | Observed Cp (kJ/(kg·K)) | Deviation (%) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 318.15 | 0.0 | 3.8680 | 3.7195 | 3.9938 |
| 318.15 | 0.358 | 3.4173 | 3.3675 | 1.4787 |
| 353.15 | 0.358 | 3.3414 | 3.4707 | -3.7256 |

2 of 3 states exceed the 3% comparison limit.

[#124](https://github.com/tannerpolley/Amine-Thermodynamics/issues/124) fixes these misses before the joint refit, starting with the water parameters. The unloaded 80 °C value is [#161](https://github.com/tannerpolley/Amine-Thermodynamics/issues/161); no current value for it or for a pure-water grid is retained in this set.

# Open work

The paper ([#170](https://github.com/tannerpolley/Amine-Thermodynamics/issues/170)) is updated only after one joint MEA refit, which takes:

- [#172](https://github.com/tannerpolley/Amine-Thermodynamics/issues/172): Schreckenberg permittivity with the low-density limit;
- [#124](https://github.com/tannerpolley/Amine-Thermodynamics/issues/124): a water refit at 3% Cp without worse density, then solution Cp;
- [#182](https://github.com/tannerpolley/Amine-Thermodynamics/issues/182): fit the two Böttinger 40 °C states and Matin state 016;
- [#183](https://github.com/tannerpolley/Amine-Thermodynamics/issues/183): loaded-solution density in the physical fit;
- [#184](https://github.com/tannerpolley/Amine-Thermodynamics/issues/184): the Jakobsen D₂O dilution and loading basis.
